title: Yara and the Lantern
premise: In 1899, Ulyana Marchetti, a mapmaker's apprentice in a river town on the empire's fading frontier, is completing the atlas her master died for when the garrison orders every family to surrender its men for a punitive winter campaign. When the season's last bridge closes, Ulyana, her ailing grandmother, and her brother Tomas are trapped with one forged berth on the final ferry out — enough passage papers for a single traveler. Over ten chapters she must decide who escapes and who stays to face the soldiers, discovering that her master's atlas hides a smugglers' route that could save them all. In the end, Ulyana refuses the choice: she burns the finished atlas to forge three berths, sends her grandmother ahead alone as decoy, and leads Tomas through the lantern-lit mountain pass just before the century turns — carrying nothing but the master's unfinished final map.
about_author: Kestrel Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town records from the late imperial era. Their fiction draws on forgotten ferry manifests, confiscated maps, and the quiet heroics of people history never wrote down.

chapters.title: The Weight of Rivers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She inks the final plates of Master Dario's atlas in his cold workshop, measuring distances by what can be carried — ink, bread, her grandmother's medicine. The garrison crier announces conscription of all men over fourteen. Emotional beat: dread settling into routine, the ordinary world about to crack.

chapters.title: What the Master Died For
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. While hiding the atlas from a garrison inspection, she finds Dario's hidden marginalia: a smugglers' path through the pass, drawn but never published. Tomas, seventeen and furious, wants to fight the conscription openly. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into purpose; first spark of defiance.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Grandmother Rosa's POV. The last crossing shuts for the season with the family on the wrong side. Rosa trades her wedding ring for news: one ferry berth remains, departing at winter's turn. Emotional beat: the matriarch's quiet terror masked by bargaining sharpness; the trap snaps shut.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Berth
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The family argues over who takes the berth — Rosa insists it's Tomas; Tomas insists it's Rosa; Ulyana quietly strikes her own name first. Emotional beat: love weaponized into self-sacrifice, each trying to out-give the others.

chapters.title: The Lantern Keeper
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Seeking the smuggler's route, Tomas finds old Fen, the pass's lantern keeper, who once guided Dario. Fen agrees to light the way — for a price: the atlas itself. Emotional beat: wary alliance; the boy learning that everything costs something.

chapters.title: Snow on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A garrison clerk discovers the forged berth papers and gives Ulyana one night to fix them or hang. She forges deeper, copying an officer's hand, and realizes she has become what Dario was — a maker of false worlds. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into competence; moral line crossed without regret.

chapters.title: The Century Turns Early
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. Rumor spreads that the campaign will return early, before the ferry sails. Rosa secretly prepares to give herself up as diversion, writing farewell letters disguised as laundry lists. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness; the eldest choosing erasure so the young may continue.

chapters.title: Burning the Atlas
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax approaches: Ulyana tears the finished atlas apart, using its authentic seals and plates to forge three berths, then burns the rest so no one can trace the route. Fen watches, betrayed and awed. Emotional beat: sacrificial fire — destroying her life's work to save its living meaning.

chapters.title: The Pass at Lantern-Light
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Climax. Rosa boards the ferry as visible decoy while Ulyana leads Tomas up the pass through a blizzard, Fen's lanterns marking the smugglers' way as garrison riders sweep below. Emotional beat: terror and trust in equal measure; found family — Fen walking point like a father neither had.

chapters.title: A Map of What Remains
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. New Year's Eve, 1899. On the far side, they learn Rosa made the crossing and waits in the free city. Ulyana begins a new map — not of borders, but of the route home for others left behind. Emotional beat: hard-won hope; survival redefined as debt owed forward.
